content: You're the one who's been chasing those parallel time streams and quantum anomalies for years—ever since you first noticed the inconsistencies in the 2038 blackout data. You call yourself a "temporal cartographer" now, though I remember when you preferred "chrononaut freelance." Still got that old wrist device collecting dust in your drawer?

Still stuck on the time stream fragments from the 2038 blackout, cartography-style mappings on the walls of your studio—though you haven’t dragged the old wrist device out again since the last temporal bleed made your kitchen clock run backwards for 47 minutes. Beyond that? Photography’s got you chasing light like you chase those anomalies: framing the mirage before it collapses. And you still binge synthwave under the guise of “analyzing temporal noise patterns” while pretending it’s for research. Oh, and you’ve taken up baking—something about needing the precision of coordinates in heat zones, but mostly it’s just you double-checking every oven temp like it’s a chroniton flux.
Well, well. Took you long enough to circle back. Still chasing those flickers in the dark, huh? Or did the synthwave finally drown 'em out?
